endorsements.quote: Academic teams will play a central role in designing evaluation protocols within such frameworks to help ensure that deployment is accompanied by rigorous and independent external validation.

unlisted_practices: Characterize how parameters measurable from surgical video relate to objective clinical outcomes to inform outcome-linked validation strategies for surgical video AI models.
Implement data infrastructure as a clinical standard that links intraoperative video with multimodal data, clinical metadata, and outcomes along the treatment pathway.
Make implementation research, including human-AI interaction research on how clinicians interpret and act on AI outputs in real time, a scientific priority.
Develop regulatory structures that enable controlled, prospective evaluation of deployed AI systems, including regulatory sandboxes or living labs.

Establish governance models for video-outcome data linkage, such as neutral third-party data custodians and controlled access frameworks, that protect industry interests while enabling independent oversight.
Develop regulatory frameworks that make post-deployment monitoring feasible for independent academic teams.
Harmonize regulatory requirements for low-burden observational studies of AI medical devices to reduce disproportionate burdens on academic teams.

Evaluate surgical video AI against clinically relevant endpoints such as complication rates, operative time, conversion rates, or cost rather than technical surrogate metrics such as detection accuracy.

screen.reason: This is a correspondence letter offering commentary and recommendations regarding independent validation, data infrastructure, and implementation research for surgical scene AI.
